board.note: Nothing was ticked off the last board, so its five lines are here on their second and final showing — after this they are answered and retired. The four new ones come from hunting the shape of the only line you have kept from me: an argument about how things actually get built, not a fine sentiment about it. Hirschman's 1967 essay is the find, and it is strange in a way I did not expect — it argues that we take on hard projects only because we misjudge them, and that the misjudgement is what turns a cautious person into someone who can bear risk. The Danish door stayed shut: Bohr's Open Letter to the United Nations is behind five dead links and a borrowing-only scan, so there is nothing from it here rather than something half-checked.
